title: Elder Nun Abhayā: O fearless nun! This body is so fragile — Worldlings here, Delighting, are often lustful. I will abandon this body, Mindful and…
content:
Elder Nun Abhayā:

O fearless nun!
This body is so fragile —
Worldlings here,
Delighting, are often lustful.
I will abandon this body,
Mindful and clearly comprehending.

Without heedlessness, I will strive,
I will strive to escape the painful state.
With craving destroyed, I have attained —
Accomplishing the Buddha’s teaching.

title: “One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I…
content: “One who clings, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.” - “I understand, Blessed One! I understand, Well-gone One!” - “How, monk, do you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement?” - “One who clings to form, venerable sir, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. Venerable sir, I understand in detail the meaning of the Blessed One’s brief statement thus.” - “Good, good, monk! Good, monk! Thus you understand in detail the meaning of my brief statement. One who clings to form, monk, is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One. One who clings to feeling … to perception … to formations … to consciousness is bound by Māra. One who does not cling is freed from the Evil One.”

title: “And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk called an arahant? He has made distant evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is an arahant.”

title: “Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights…
content: “Monks, one who delights in the eye delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And, monks, one who does not delight in the eye does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … the mind does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

title: “Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and…
content: “Monks, suppose there is a bitter gourd mixed with poison. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Someone says to him: ‘Good man, this bitter gourd is mixed with poison. If you wish, eat it. While eating, you will not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, you may meet death or deadly suffering.’ That man might eat it without reflection, without refusal. While eating, he does not find delight in its color, smell, or taste. After eating, he meets death or deadly suffering. Monks, I say that this course of practice is like that simile — namely, a course of practice that is painful in the present and also has painful results in the future.”

title: “Monks, there are these three fires. What three? The fire of greed, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion. These, monks, are the three…
content:
“Monks, there are these three fires. What three? The fire of greed, the fire of hatred, the fire of delusion. These, monks, are the three fires.

The fire of greed burns up people
Who are intoxicated by sensual pleasures.
The fire of hatred burns up
Those who are hateful,
Who kill living beings.

The fire of delusion burns up
Those who are confused,
Not trained in the noble Dhamma.
Not understanding these fires,
People delight in personal existence.

They increase hell,
The realm of animals,
The domain of hungry ghosts,
And also the asuras —
They are not freed
From Māra’s bondage.”

title: “Here, monks, the second kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘These first ascetics and brahmins, entering and indulging, ate the bait … and have not…
content: “Here, monks, the second kind of ascetics and brahmins think: ‘These first ascetics and brahmins, entering and indulging, ate the bait … and have not escaped Māra’s power. Suppose we completely abandon the bait and the world’s offerings, abandon what is fearful, go into the forest and dwell.’ They completely abandon the bait and the world’s offerings, abandon what is fearful, go into the forest and dwell. There they become grass-eaters, millet-eaters, raw-rice eaters, Nivara-seed eaters, crust-eaters, husk-eaters, rice-scum eaters, sesame-seed eaters, grass-eaters, cow-dung eaters, forest roots and fruits eaters, fallen-fruit eaters. At the end of the summer, when water and grass become scarce, their bodies become extremely emaciated. Because their bodies become extremely emaciated, their energy for striving is exhausted. Because their energy is exhausted, their mind’s liberation is exhausted. Because their mind’s liberation is exhausted, they return to the bait cast by Māra and the world’s offerings. There they again enter, indulge, and eat those foods. By entering, indulging, and eating, they become infatuated; from infatuation, heedless; from heedlessness, subject to Māra’s will. Thus, monks, these second ascetics and brahmins have not escaped Māra’s power.”

title: “Monks, here a monk, reflecting wisely, does not consent to arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to…
content: “Monks, here a monk, reflecting wisely, does not consent to arisen sensual thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to arisen ill-will thought … does not consent to arisen harmful thought; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes it non-existent. He does not consent to any arisen evil, unwholesome states; he abandons, dispels, destroys, makes them non-existent.”

title: “This good teaching I give to you — You who have gathered here. Dig up the root of craving Like digging up birana grass. Do…
content:
“This good teaching I give to you —
You who have gathered here.
Dig up the root of craving
Like digging up birana grass.
Do not let Māra destroy you,
Like a flood destroying reeds.”

“Even though a tree is cut down,
If its root remains uncut,
The tree grows back —
So too, if the latent tendency to craving is not uprooted,
Suffering arises again and again.”

“The thirty-six streams of craving
Sweep away a person who is bent on pleasing thoughts —
Thoughts of lust,
Sweeping him away with wrong view.”

title: The inner fetter and the outer fetter — Beings are entangled in these fetters. I ask Gotama about this: Who can escape these fetters? (The…
content:
The inner fetter and the outer fetter —
Beings are entangled in these fetters.
I ask Gotama about this:
Who can escape these fetters?

(The Blessed One):
One established in virtue, wise,
Developing mind and wisdom,
Ardent and discreet —
That monk can escape the fetters.
One who has abandoned greed,
Hatred, and ignorance,
The defilement-free arahant —
He has escaped the fetters.
Where name-and-form is destroyed
Without remainder,
Where the hindrance and perceptions of form are destroyed —
There the fetters are cut.
